rows: Created issue: Cancelling run_command leaks the shell's backgrounded descendants

gate:src/tools/execution/tests.rs — run_command_cancellation_stops_backgrounded_descendants. The shell now gets its own process group via tokio process_group(0) on unix, and cancellation signals the group with rustix kill_process_group rather than relying on kill_on_drop reaching only the direct child. Red first with the shape from the issue, sh -lc "sleep 300 & echo $! > file; wait": "backgrounded descendant 430343 outlived the cancelled turn". Green after, and stress-run 30 consecutive times, all ok, rather than trusting one pass - daa-fji9 was a flaky test I wrote earlier today and did not stress. Full suite 126/320/18/1/11 green, fmt, clippy --all-targets --all-features, cargo doc and cargo audit clean. The test reads the /proc state field rather than testing directory existence, because the orphaned descendant is exactly the unreaped-zombie case daa-vh77 turned on; it is Linux-gated for that reason while the fix itself is unix-wide. rustix moved from a linux-only to a cfg(unix) dependency - no new crate, wider target. PID reuse is addressed by reading child.id() before the wait future takes ownership: the child stays unreaped until that future drops, so the kernel cannot recycle the pid onto an unrelated process before the signal. Both open questions from the description are answered in the run_command_tool_execution doc comment rather than left implicit: the terminal branch delegates descendant handling to the client via terminal/kill, and non-unix targets kill only the shell, which is now stated as a known limit instead of silently tolerated.

Created issue: Terminal cancellation can hang while awaiting editor cleanup

RED: cargo +1.95 test --locked --test serve_terminal -- --nocapture: all three shipped-binary fixtures fail. Pending-create cancellation and disconnect-owner tests time out waiting for cancelled prompt; wait-phase cancellation never attempts terminal/release after an unanswered kill. Acceptance checklist: [x] reproduce with real ACP terminal capability and deliberately withheld responses; [ ] connection-owned pending create with explicit response acceptance, late-ID cleanup and disconnect teardown; [ ] cancellation in create/wait/output; [ ] bounded kill/release with release attempted after failed kill; [ ] recovery prompt and sanitized cleanup diagnostics; [ ] existing success/failure/unit coverage; [ ] README, full gates and repeated lifecycle runs.

Completed checklist: [x] three real serve red failures; [x] connection-owned pending terminal/create with two-channel acceptance handshake so a queued response cannot lose ownership when cancellation wins; [x] late terminal IDs killed/released, unsent cancelled creates skipped, disconnect tears down the owner; [x] biased cancellation during create/wait/output; [x] one-second kill/release deadlines and release attempted even if kill fails; [x] error codes/stage diagnostics without editor payload disclosure; [x] real release-phase cancellation and post-cancel prompt recovery; [x] pre-cancelled unit test proves zero creates, existing cancellation test now cancels after creation rather than requiring a forbidden create-after-cancel; [x] README caveat about remote termination; [x] all 568 tests, fmt, Clippy -D warnings, rustdoc -D warnings, release and diff checks pass; [x] ten consecutive real terminal lifecycle suites pass. No new dependencies; prior audit/size gates remain passing.

Lesson: cancellation of a side-effectful RPC is an ownership transfer, not just dropping its future. Retain a pending create under the connection until the caller explicitly accepts its returned identity; otherwise clean up the late terminal. Cleanup itself must be bounded and must not skip release on kill failure. A nonresponsive remote editor cannot be forced to terminate its process by local deadlines; document that limit honestly.
Owned late terminal creation and bounded cleanup verified over real ACP with withheld replies

Scope change (maintainer decision 2026-10-10, during .1): the v2 spec's baseline is all-or-nothing. Advertising session: {} MUST cover session/new, list, resume, close, prompt, cancel, update, and prompts MUST accept ContentBlock::Text and ContentBlock::ResourceLink (https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v2/initialization, Agent/Session Capabilities). The confirmed cut omitted load/resume and close; a probe advertising them without implementing them would be non-conformant. Decision: expand to the baseline. .3 adds session/resume (v2 merges load+resume, incl. optional history replay; map to the existing v1 load/resume in the session store), session/close (existing v1 close), and ResourceLink prompt blocks turned into text for the model (no fetching). MCP, edits, terminals stay out (optional capabilities). .1 advertises session: {} without mcp/prompt extensions. Refs claude/b9707559-6fe1-42c2-94af-e24e2b00aec8

Candidate findings so far (for .5 docs/protocol-v2.md; none filed yet):
1. Baseline is all-or-nothing: advertising session {} obliges resume and close (and ResourceLink prompts). An agent without persistence cannot expose sessions at all. Possibly intended; worth asking whether a narrower baseline was considered.
2. Ordering ambiguity: the SDK example sends a ready idle state_update after session/new's response; a client that waits for 'idle' after sending its first prompt can mistake that ready idle for turn completion (our own wire test hit this race). The spec could state that completion is the idle that follows the running transition after acceptance (the SDK example says so in a comment).
3. SDK docs: Agent.protocol_router() exists (role/acp.rs) but the README only documents Proxy.protocol_router(); agent authors may not find the side-by-side v1/v2 entry point.
4. Stop rule held through .3: the turn loop needed no change beyond the admission event; message IDs come from the shared derived_message_id (acp layer).
Not upstream: SDK 3.1/schema 1.10.2 lacked the error stop reason (#2281); fixed by upgrading to 3.3.0/1.11.0 (.8). Refs claude/b9707559-6fe1-42c2-94af-e24e2b00aec8

More candidate findings (.4): 5. v2 permission requests carry the subject's ToolCallUpdate, so a diff preview needs the new v2 diff format; our probe sends none for edits, a regression vs v1 0.9.3 previews until the v2 diff is implemented. 6. CommandPermissionSubject (command, cwd, toolCallId) fits run_command better than a generic tool_call subject; not used yet. 7. SetSessionConfigOptionRequest flattens the value (type/value at the request top level) while ConfigOptionUpdate/response nest options - easy to get wrong; our own test did. Implemented and verified the exact offline audit reproduction at the shipped serve/HTTP boundary. Selected-content requests carry without_retries through LlmClient; SSE and reqwest retries plus completion redirects cannot bypass the one-POST limit. Ordinary transport recovery retains three pre-output retries (100/200/400 ms), clamps server retry directives, never resets its budget after a long empty connection, and stops after any normalized completion event. Finished generations may end without a separate DONE marker. The returned stream owns its transport JoinSet; cancellation, receiver closure or drop releases pending HTTP responses. No new dependency or transport framework. Lesson: a Model-request budget must constrain the physical HTTP sender, including hidden client retry/redirect behavior; counting harness or fake LlmClient calls cannot prove it. Keep normalized output exposure as the replay cutoff and bind background transport lifetime to the returned stream. src/tools/execution/mod.rs:1138-1157 maps the delegated preflight read to Some and propagates every error; :438 aborts the write. Negative check: assert the actual fs/write_text_file request, target/content and resulting file; a tool-only success assertion is not sufficient.

Because neither live backend could complete a turn, the refactor that collapsed

Gates: 489 tests pass (baseline 484 + 5 new, 0 failures), `cargo fmt --check`,
`cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings`, `cargo doc` with
`RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings`, and `scripts/check-agent-instructions` all green.

Note for review: the published Groq rates ($0.15/$0.75 per M for gpt-oss-120b,
$0.075/$0.30 for gpt-oss-20b) were transcribed from Groq's pricing page, not
fetched from an API — there is no pricing endpoint. The context windows *were*
taken from Groq's live `GET /models` payload. If the rates drift, `LLM_PRICING`
overrides them without a recompile.

## Lesson

The context windows in this change were correct because they were read from
Groq's live `GET /models` payload. The prices were wrong because they were
written from memory instead — gpt-oss-120b output was off by 25%, and the code
asserted Groq had no prompt-cache tier when it bills cache reads at half the
input rate. Both errors survived a green suite, because the tests asserted the
same remembered numbers the implementation used: a table and a test that agree
prove consistency, not accuracy.

The existing rule in docs/agent-rust.md covers third-party *crate* docs ("look
up a third-party crate's current documentation rather than guessing at method
signatures or feature flags"). It does not cover third-party *provider* facts —
prices, context windows, model ids — which are equally external, change more
often, and unlike a wrong method signature do not fail to compile.

Worth considering as an instruction amendment: any provider constant committed
to a table cites the page or API response it came from, and is fetched at the
time of writing rather than recalled. Left as a suggestion here rather than an
edit to the contract, which is the maintainer's to change.

## Closing evidence

Rates now cite the per-model pages
(<https://console.groq.com/docs/model/openai/gpt-oss-120b>, and the 20b
equivalent). Corrected in 278461d and verified live: a 431-input/27-output turn
reports $0.000080, matching 431 * $0.15/M + 27 * $0.60/M computed by hand.

Full acceptance as filed: `--backend groq` is listed in `serve --help`; a Groq
session emits `usage_update` with `size: 131072` and an accruing cost; suite
(489 tests), fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo doc` and the instruction size
check all green.

Two follow-ups were filed rather than folded in: daa-models-context-window-9cr3
(prefer the provider's own `/models` context_window over the static table) and
daa-base-url-desync-sx0r (P1 — `LLM_BASE_URL` is ignored by the model fetch,
found while verifying this work).

Created issue: Dependency audit retains unsound event-listener and yanked chacha20 warnings

gate:cargo audit — now reports nothing at all, where it previously ended with "2 allowed warnings found". Both resolved by semver-compatible patch bumps in Cargo.lock, no manifest change and no source change: event-listener 5.4.1 to 5.4.2 and chacha20 0.10.1 to 0.10.2. Full suite 126/320/18/1/11 green, fmt, clippy --all-targets --all-features, cargo doc and cargo build --release all clean, so the protocol tests the issue asked to preserve are intact. Applicability, which the issue asked for rather than a blind bump: RUSTSEC-2026-0221 requires Event::with_tag with a !Send tag type and a StackSlot crossing threads. Neither with_tag nor StackSlot appears anywhere in the crates between us and event-listener - blocking 1.7.0, async-process 2.5.0, async-lock 3.4.2, async-channel 2.5.0 - and this crate never names event-listener itself, so the unsoundness was not reachable in this graph. It is fixed because the fix was free, not because it was exploitable here. chacha20 0.10.1 carried no vulnerability either; yanked means the author withdrew it, so the cost was resolution fragility rather than risk. Worth noting for whoever reads this next: cargo audit exits 0 for the warning classes, unsound and yanked, so neither finding could ever have failed CI. That is why they sat long enough to need an issue. Raised with the maintainer as a separate decision rather than changed here, since --deny warnings turns any future upstream yank into a red build at an arbitrary moment.

Created issue: Proxy survives client death in two lifecycle scenarios

Diagnosis in the description is wrong. The proxy does not survive client death — it exits correctly and reaps every descendant. The test misreads an unreaped exit status as a live process.

## Evidence

Sampling /proc/<pid>/stat field 3 for every recorded role while the test runs:

    parent_death_does_not_depend_on_client_stdin_reaching_eof
      client  GONE
      proxy   Z      ppid=141502
      agent   GONE
      worker  GONE
      leaf    GONE
      holder  S      ppid=141502   (expected to survive)

    client_death_reaps_detached_descendants_without_touching_another_session
      killed tree:    client GONE, proxy Z, agent GONE, worker GONE, leaf GONE
      neighbour tree: all five S                    (correctly untouched)

The proxy is a **zombie**, and its whole subtree is gone. That is the reap path working. Reproduced by hand outside the harness too: build the tree, `kill -9` the client, and agent/worker/leaf disappear while client and proxy linger as `ZN`.

## Root cause

tests/lifecycle/mod.rs:109 defined liveness as directory existence:

    fn alive(pid: u32) -> bool {
        std::path::Path::new(&format!("/proc/{pid}")).exists()
    }

The kernel keeps /proc/<pid> until someone reaps the exit status. Both failing tests SIGKILL the proxy's parent, so no one is left to reap the proxy; it is reparented to the nearest subreaper and stays a zombie for as long as that subreaper declines to collect it. On this machine an ancestor subreaper (pid 141502) never reaps, so the zombie outlives the test's 5s deadline every time. Under an ancestry whose reaper collects promptly — a container with a reaping PID 1 — the window is too short to observe, which is why CI is green.

The three lifecycle tests that pass are exactly the three where someone reaps the proxy: proxy_termination and wrapped_agent_exit leave the client fixture alive to `wait()` on it, and client_eof_bounds makes the test process itself the proxy's parent. The two that fail are exactly the two that kill the parent. The pattern fits the zombie explanation and nothing else.

## Correction to the premise

daa-30py claimed these two failures were stale-fixture noise; I claimed they were a real reap defect from 9817a88. Both were wrong. 9817a88's fix is sound and its coverage was not red when it merged — it is red only under a process ancestry that does not reap orphans.

Created issue: acp-proxy never exits when the wrapped agent process exits before completing the ACP handshake

Root cause: main() returned ExitCode after the wrapped child exited. #[tokio::main]
drops the Runtime on return, which blocks until every spawn_blocking task finishes.
The stdin-forwarding pump reads via tokio::io::stdin(), a spawn_blocking thread doing
a real blocking read() on the proxy's own stdin. .abort() cancels the async wrapper
but cannot interrupt that OS-level blocking read, so if anything (a pipe, a terminal,
a real client) still holds the proxy's stdin open when the wrapped child dies,
Runtime::drop hangs forever even though wait_for_child() returned promptly.

Fix: main() now calls std::process::exit() directly instead of returning ExitCode,
bypassing the runtime's blocking-pool drain on shutdown. #[allow(clippy::exit)]
added with justification.

The shell now gets its own process group via tokio process_group(0) on unix, and cancellation signals the group with rustix kill_process_group rather than relying on kill_on_drop reaching only the direct child. Red first with the shape from the issue, sh -lc "sleep 300 & echo $! > file; wait": "backgrounded descendant 430343 outlived the cancelled turn". Green after, and stress-run 30 consecutive times, all ok, rather than trusting one pass - daa-fji9 was a flaky test I wrote earlier today and did not stress. The test reads the /proc state field rather than testing directory existence, because the orphaned descendant is exactly the unreaped-zombie case daa-vh77 turned on; it is Linux-gated for that reason while the fix itself is unix-wide. rustix moved from a linux-only to a cfg(unix) dependency - no new crate, wider target. PID reuse is addressed by reading child.id() before the wait future takes ownership: the child stays unreaped until that future drops, so the kernel cannot recycle the pid onto an unrelated process before the signal. Both open questions from the description are answered in the run_command_tool_execution doc comment rather than left implicit: the terminal branch delegates descendant handling to the client via terminal/kill, and non-unix targets kill only the shell, which is now stated as a known limit instead of silently tolerated.

Created issue: ACP v2 support alongside v1 (per-connection negotiation)

Scope change (maintainer decision 2026-10-10, during .1): the v2 spec's baseline is all-or-nothing. Advertising session: {} MUST cover session/new, list, resume, close, prompt, cancel, update, and prompts MUST accept ContentBlock::Text and ContentBlock::ResourceLink (https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v2/initialization, Agent/Session Capabilities). The confirmed cut omitted load/resume and close; a probe advertising them without implementing them would be non-conformant. Decision: expand to the baseline. .3 adds session/resume (v2 merges load+resume, incl. optional history replay; map to the existing v1 load/resume in the session store), session/close (existing v1 close), and ResourceLink prompt blocks turned into text for the model (no fetching). MCP, edits, terminals stay out (optional capabilities). .1 advertises session: {} without mcp/prompt extensions. Refs claude/b9707559-6fe1-42c2-94af-e24e2b00aec8

Candidate findings so far (for .5 docs/protocol-v2.md; none filed yet):
1. Baseline is all-or-nothing: advertising session {} obliges resume and close (and ResourceLink prompts). An agent without persistence cannot expose sessions at all. Possibly intended; worth asking whether a narrower baseline was considered.
2. Ordering ambiguity: the SDK example sends a ready idle state_update after session/new's response; a client that waits for 'idle' after sending its first prompt can mistake that ready idle for turn completion (our own wire test hit this race). The spec could state that completion is the idle that follows the running transition after acceptance (the SDK example says so in a comment).
3. SDK docs: Agent.protocol_router() exists (role/acp.rs) but the README only documents Proxy.protocol_router(); agent authors may not find the side-by-side v1/v2 entry point.
4. Stop rule held through .3: the turn loop needed no change beyond the admission event; message IDs come from the shared derived_message_id (acp layer).
Not upstream: SDK 3.1/schema 1.10.2 lacked the error stop reason (#2281); fixed by upgrading to 3.3.0/1.11.0 (.8). Refs claude/b9707559-6fe1-42c2-94af-e24e2b00aec8

More candidate findings (.4): 5. v2 permission requests carry the subject's ToolCallUpdate, so a diff preview needs the new v2 diff format; our probe sends none for edits, a regression vs v1 0.9.3 previews until the v2 diff is implemented. 6. CommandPermissionSubject (command, cwd, toolCallId) fits run_command better than a generic tool_call subject; not used yet. 7. SetSessionConfigOptionRequest flattens the value (type/value at the request top level) while ConfigOptionUpdate/response nest options - easy to get wrong; our own test did. Refs claude/b9707559-6fe1-42c2-94af-e24e2b00aec8

Implemented and verified the exact offline audit reproduction at the shipped serve/HTTP boundary. Selected-content requests carry without_retries through LlmClient; SSE and reqwest retries plus completion redirects cannot bypass the one-POST limit. Ordinary transport recovery retains three pre-output retries (100/200/400 ms), clamps server retry directives, never resets its budget after a long empty connection, and stops after any normalized completion event. Finished generations may end without a separate DONE marker. The returned stream owns its transport JoinSet; cancellation, receiver closure or drop releases pending HTTP responses. No new dependency or transport framework. Lesson: a Model-request budget must constrain the physical HTTP sender, including hidden client retry/redirect behavior; counting harness or fake LlmClient calls cannot prove it. Note for review: the published Groq rates ($0.15/$0.75 per M for gpt-oss-120b,
$0.075/$0.30 for gpt-oss-20b) were transcribed from Groq's pricing page, not
fetched from an API — there is no pricing endpoint. The context windows *were*
taken from Groq's live `GET /models` payload. If the rates drift, `LLM_PRICING`
overrides them without a recompile.

## Lesson

The context windows in this change were correct because they were read from
Groq's live `GET /models` payload. The prices were wrong because they were
written from memory instead — gpt-oss-120b output was off by 25%, and the code
asserted Groq had no prompt-cache tier when it bills cache reads at half the
input rate. Both errors survived a green suite, because the tests asserted the
same remembered numbers the implementation used: a table and a test that agree
prove consistency, not accuracy.

The existing rule in docs/agent-rust.md covers third-party *crate* docs ("look
up a third-party crate's current documentation rather than guessing at method
signatures or feature flags"). It does not cover third-party *provider* facts —
prices, context windows, model ids — which are equally external, change more
often, and unlike a wrong method signature do not fail to compile.

Worth considering as an instruction amendment: any provider constant committed
to a table cites the page or API response it came from, and is fetched at the
time of writing rather than recalled. Left as a suggestion here rather than an
edit to the contract, which is the maintainer's to change.

## Closing evidence

(<https://console.groq.com/docs/model/openai/gpt-oss-120b>, and the 20b
equivalent). Corrected in 278461d and verified live: a 431-input/27-output turn
reports $0.000080, matching 431 * $0.15/M + 27 * $0.60/M computed by hand.

check all green.

Created issue: Dependency audit retains unsound event-listener and yanked chacha20 warnings

gate:cargo audit — now reports nothing at all, where it previously ended with "2 allowed warnings found". Both resolved by semver-compatible patch bumps in Cargo.lock, no manifest change and no source change: event-listener 5.4.1 to 5.4.2 and chacha20 0.10.1 to 0.10.2. Full suite 126/320/18/1/11 green, fmt, clippy --all-targets --all-features, cargo doc and cargo build --release all clean, so the protocol tests the issue asked to preserve are intact. Applicability, which the issue asked for rather than a blind bump: RUSTSEC-2026-0221 requires Event::with_tag with a !Send tag type and a StackSlot crossing threads. Neither with_tag nor StackSlot appears anywhere in the crates between us and event-listener - blocking 1.7.0, async-process 2.5.0, async-lock 3.4.2, async-channel 2.5.0 - and this crate never names event-listener itself, so the unsoundness was not reachable in this graph. It is fixed because the fix was free, not because it was exploitable here. chacha20 0.10.1 carried no vulnerability either; yanked means the author withdrew it, so the cost was resolution fragility rather than risk. Worth noting for whoever reads this next: cargo audit exits 0 for the warning classes, unsound and yanked, so neither finding could ever have failed CI. That is why they sat long enough to need an issue. Raised with the maintainer as a separate decision rather than changed here, since --deny warnings turns any future upstream yank into a red build at an arbitrary moment.

Created issue: Proxy survives client death in two lifecycle scenarios

Diagnosis in the description is wrong. The proxy does not survive client death — it exits correctly and reaps every descendant. The test misreads an unreaped exit status as a live process.

## Evidence

Sampling /proc/<pid>/stat field 3 for every recorded role while the test runs:

    parent_death_does_not_depend_on_client_stdin_reaching_eof
      client  GONE
      proxy   Z      ppid=141502
      agent   GONE
      worker  GONE
      leaf    GONE
      holder  S      ppid=141502   (expected to survive)

    client_death_reaps_detached_descendants_without_touching_another_session
      killed tree:    client GONE, proxy Z, agent GONE, worker GONE, leaf GONE
      neighbour tree: all five S                    (correctly untouched)

The proxy is a **zombie**, and its whole subtree is gone. That is the reap path working. Reproduced by hand outside the harness too: build the tree, `kill -9` the client, and agent/worker/leaf disappear while client and proxy linger as `ZN`.

## Root cause

tests/lifecycle/mod.rs:109 defined liveness as directory existence:

    fn alive(pid: u32) -> bool {
        std::path::Path::new(&format!("/proc/{pid}")).exists()
    }

The kernel keeps /proc/<pid> until someone reaps the exit status. Both failing tests SIGKILL the proxy's parent, so no one is left to reap the proxy; it is reparented to the nearest subreaper and stays a zombie for as long as that subreaper declines to collect it. On this machine an ancestor subreaper (pid 141502) never reaps, so the zombie outlives the test's 5s deadline every time. Under an ancestry whose reaper collects promptly — a container with a reaping PID 1 — the window is too short to observe, which is why CI is green.

The three lifecycle tests that pass are exactly the three where someone reaps the proxy: proxy_termination and wrapped_agent_exit leave the client fixture alive to `wait()` on it, and client_eof_bounds makes the test process itself the proxy's parent. The two that fail are exactly the two that kill the parent. The pattern fits the zombie explanation and nothing else.

## Correction to the premise

daa-30py claimed these two failures were stale-fixture noise; I claimed they were a real reap defect from 9817a88. Both were wrong. 9817a88's fix is sound and its coverage was not red when it merged — it is red only under a process ancestry that does not reap orphans.

Created issue: acp-proxy never exits when the wrapped agent process exits before completing the ACP handshake

Root cause: main() returned ExitCode after the wrapped child exited. #[tokio::main]
drops the Runtime on return, which blocks until every spawn_blocking task finishes.
The stdin-forwarding pump reads via tokio::io::stdin(), a spawn_blocking thread doing
a real blocking read() on the proxy's own stdin. .abort() cancels the async wrapper
but cannot interrupt that OS-level blocking read, so if anything (a pipe, a terminal,
a real client) still holds the proxy's stdin open when the wrapped child dies,
Runtime::drop hangs forever even though wait_for_child() returned promptly.

Fix: main() now calls std::process::exit() directly instead of returning ExitCode,
bypassing the runtime's blocking-pool drain on shutdown. #[allow(clippy::exit)]
added with justification.

Created issue: Local run_command ignores cancellation without ACP terminal support

gate:src/tools/execution/tests.rs — the no-terminal branch now spawns through tokio::process::Command with kill_on_drop and selects on the cancellation token, matching the terminal branch contract: kill the command, return ToolExecution::failed("run_command cancelled"). Red first and measured: run_command_without_terminal_support_honours_an_already_cancelled_turn and _stops_a_command_cancelled_mid_flight both failed with "run_command ignored the cancelled token and waited for the command" and the target took 30.01s, the full sleep 30; after the fix the same tests pass in 0.20s. Also removes the blocking-task hazard the issue described: there is no spawn_blocking job left for runtime shutdown to wait on. Two pieces of the acceptance are deliberately NOT met and are filed rather than glossed: daa-0yi0, cancellation kills the shell but not its backgrounded descendants, proven with a standalone reproduction where sh dies and the grandchild survives - fixing it needs process groups and a non-Linux decision, a different change from this one; and daa-wu5e, the serve-level verification with a live command could not be written at all because MockLlmClient never emits a tool call, so no test can drive a real serve process into run_command. What is proven here is that the function honours cancellation promptly; what is not proven is the end-to-end serve shutdown path the issue also asked about.
